Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses, speaking.
translations.2: Command the sons of Israel, and say to them: When you enter the land of your dwelling, which I am giving you,
translations.3: and you offer an offering to God — a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill gift, or at your festivals — and you intend it to be accepted and pleasing to God, from the cattle or from the flock,
translations.4: then the one who brings that offering shall bring with it, from grain, a tenth of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a qist of oil;
translations.5: and wine for the libation — a quarter of a qist — you shall make it with the burnt offering or with the sacrifice, for the one lamb.
translations.6: And for the ram you shall bring, from grain, two tenths of fine flour mixed with a third of a qist of oil;
translations.7: and wine for the libation — a third of a qist — you shall offer it, accepted and pleasing to God.
translations.8: And when you make from the cattle a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a peace-offering to God,
translations.9: then he shall bring with it, from grain, three tenths of fine flour mixed with half a qist of oil;
translations.10: and wine — offer it for the libation — half a qist, accepted and pleasing to God.
translations.11: So shall it be done with every ox, and with every ram, and with every head from the sheep or from the goats.
translations.12: According to the count of what you offer of them, so shall you do with each one of those counted.
translations.13: So shall every native-born do, when he brings an offering accepted and pleasing to God.
translations.14: And any sojourner who has come among you, or who has dwelt in your midst throughout the passing of your generations, and has made an offering and intended it to be accepted and pleasing to God — just as you do, so shall he do.
translations.15: O assembly! One ordinance for you and for the stranger who has come in — an eternal ordinance throughout the passing of your generations, for the stranger is as you are before God.
translations.16: So likewise: one law and one ruling shall be for you and for the stranger who has come in among you.
translations.17: Then God spoke to Moses, speaking.
translations.18: Command the sons of Israel, and say to them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you there,
translations.19: then whenever you eat of the food of the land, raise up a heave-offering to God.
translations.20: The first of your dough — a loaf-cake you shall raise up as a heave-offering, like the heave-offering of the threshing-floor; so shall you raise it up.
translations.21: And likewise, the first of your dough you shall make for God a heave-offering, throughout the passing of your generations.
translations.22: And if you have erred, and have not carried out all these commandments which God commanded Moses —
translations.23: like all that God commanded you by the hand of Moses, from the day He began the command, and onward throughout the passing of your generations —
translations.24: then if the error was away from the eyes of the assembly, they shall make a bull from the cattle — a burnt offering, accepted and pleasing to God — and with it grain and libation as required, and a he-goat from the goats for the purification-offering.
translations.25: And he shall seek forgiveness for them, since that was an error, and they have brought their burnt offering as an offering to God, and their purification-offering for their lapse.
translations.26: And it shall be forgiven to the assembly of the sons of Israel and to the stranger who has come in among them, since all the people acted in error.
translations.27: And if a single person errs likewise, in error, he shall offer a ewe-lamb in its first year for the purification-offering.
translations.28: And the imām shall seek forgiveness on behalf of that erring person, for what he erred in error before God; and it shall be forgiven him and pardoned from him.
translations.29: For the native-born among the sons of Israel, and the stranger who has come in among them — one law shall be for you, for whoever errs in error.
translations.30: But any person who does that with a high hand, whether native-born or sojourner — he is a blasphemer against his Lord; that person shall be cut off from among his people.
translations.31: Because he has despised the word of God and broken His covenant — that person shall surely be cut off; his iniquity is upon him.
translations.32: And when the sons of Israel were dwelling in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood for himself on the Sabbath day.
translations.33: And those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron, and the rest of the assembly.
translations.34: And they placed him in custody, because it had not been made clear to them what should be done with him.
translations.35: And God said to Moses: The man shall surely be put to death — and that by the whole assembly stoning him with stones, outside the camp.
translations.36: And they brought him out outside the camp, and stoned him with stones until he died — as God had commanded Moses.
translations.37: And God said to Moses, saying:
translations.38: Command the sons of Israel and say to them that they shall make for themselves a fringe upon the edges of their outer garments, throughout the passing of their generations; and they shall place upon the fringe of the edge a thread of blue-violet wool.
translations.39: And that shall be for you a visible fringe — you shall see it and remember all the commandments of God and do them; and you shall not seek to follow your hearts and your eyes, after which you go astray.
translations.40: So that you may remember that always, and do all My commandments — and you shall be consecrated to your Lord.
translations.41: I am God your Lord, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, to be your God. I am God your Lord, everlasting in existence.
